_comment: Shared cross-language cases for the two returnTo sanitizers.
THE CONTRACT: sanitizeOAuthReturnTo (Go, the Google sign-in round trip)
and sanitizeReturnTo (TypeScript, the auth page) return the same string
for every input, so a Google sign-in lands where the other sign-in methods
do, and the auth page never keeps a destination the backend refuses. The
rules, and the reason for each, are documented on sanitizeOAuthReturnTo.
Go reads this file in oauth_return_to_test.go (package auth, beside this
testdata folder); TypeScript reads it in
frontend/app/auth/auth-redirect-utils.test.ts. Each asserts its own
sanitizer's exact output against `want` for every case and pins its own
fallback constant to `fallback`, so a rule changed on one side fails that
side's suite and names the input. A rule this file carries no case for is
a rule it cannot police, so add cases with rules.
fallback         = what both sanitizers return for a refused input, and
also what they return for "/".
maxLength        = the length cap both sanitizers apply. The Go suite pins
oauthReturnToMaxLength to it and requires a kept case of
exactly this length and a refused case one past it.
cases[].input    = the raw value each sanitizer is handed.
cases[].want     = both sanitizers' exact return value.
cases[].rule     = the rule the case exercises.

cases.name: on-site path
cases.rule: a same-origin path passes unchanged

cases.name: site root
cases.rule: a same-origin path passes unchanged

cases.name: path with query
cases.rule: a same-origin path passes unchanged

cases.name: path with query and fragment
cases.rule: a same-origin path passes unchanged

cases.name: path with fragment
cases.rule: a same-origin path passes unchanged

cases.name: percent-encoded path
cases.rule: a same-origin path passes unchanged

cases.name: query carrying separators
cases.rule: a same-origin path passes unchanged

cases.name: a path that only starts with auth
cases.rule: not the sign-in page or anything under it

cases.name: backslash in the query
cases.rule: the path rules do not apply to the query or fragment

cases.name: backslash in the fragment
cases.rule: the path rules do not apply to the query or fragment

cases.name: dot-dot in the query only
cases.rule: the path rules do not apply to the query or fragment

cases.name: encoded slash inside a segment
cases.rule: a segment is a dot segment only when it decodes to exactly . or ..

cases.name: at the length limit
cases.rule: length cap of 2048 characters

cases.name: empty
cases.rule: only a path: a value that does not start with / is refused

cases.name: relative path
cases.rule: only a path: a value that does not start with / is refused

cases.name: absolute URL
cases.rule: only a same-origin path: a scheme or host is refused

cases.name: absolute URL with path
cases.rule: only a same-origin path: a scheme or host is refused

cases.name: scheme only
cases.rule: only a same-origin path: a scheme or host is refused

cases.name: protocol-relative
cases.rule: no leading //: it is protocol-relative

cases.name: protocol-relative with path
cases.rule: no leading //: it is protocol-relative

cases.name: backslash after slash
cases.rule: no backslash in the path: a browser reads it as /

cases.name: tab inside
cases.rule: printable ASCII only: a browser strips a tab, which here leaves a protocol-relative //host

cases.name: dot-dot segment
cases.rule: no . or .. path segment, including one that resolves onto the sign-in page

cases.name: encoded dot-dot segment
cases.rule: no . or .. path segment, including one that resolves onto the sign-in page

cases.name: dot-dot into protocol-relative
cases.rule: no . or .. path segment, including one that resolves the path into a protocol-relative //host

cases.name: dot then dot-dot into protocol-relative
cases.rule: no . or .. path segment, including one that resolves the path into a protocol-relative //host

cases.name: dot-dot after a segment into protocol-relative
cases.rule: no . or .. path segment, including one that resolves the path into a protocol-relative //host

cases.name: dot-dot into protocol-relative with path and query
cases.rule: no . or .. path segment, including one that resolves the path into a protocol-relative //host

cases.name: auth page
cases.rule: not the sign-in page or anything under it

cases.name: auth page with query
cases.rule: not the sign-in page or anything under it

cases.name: auth page with an unencoded returnTo
cases.rule: not the sign-in page or anything under it

cases.name: under the auth page
cases.rule: not the sign-in page or anything under it

cases.name: under the auth page with query
cases.rule: not the sign-in page or anything under it

cases.name: backslash later in the path
cases.rule: no backslash in the path: a browser reads it as /

cases.name: dot segment
cases.rule: no . or .. path segment

cases.name: dot-dot segment between on-site paths
cases.rule: no . or .. path segment

cases.name: newline inside
cases.rule: printable ASCII only

cases.name: space inside
cases.rule: printable ASCII only

cases.name: leading space
cases.rule: printable ASCII only

cases.name: non-ASCII character
cases.rule: printable ASCII only

cases.name: undecodable segment
cases.rule: every percent escape in the path and fragment decodes

cases.name: undecodable fragment
cases.rule: every percent escape in the path and fragment decodes

cases.name: encoded spelling of the auth page
cases.rule: not the sign-in page or anything under it

cases.name: too long
cases.rule: length cap of 2048 characters

cases.name: undecodable escape in the query
cases.rule: a malformed percent escape in the query passes: neither sanitizer decodes the query

cases.name: escape that is not UTF-8
cases.rule: a well-formed percent escape passes whether or not its bytes are UTF-8

cases.name: encoded backslash
cases.rule: an encoded backslash passes: a browser does not read %5C as a slash

cases.name: dots inside a segment
cases.rule: a segment holding dots and other characters is not a dot segment

cases.name: mixed encoded dot-dot segment
cases.rule: no . or .. path segment, percent-encoded or not

cases.name: encoded slash into the auth page
cases.rule: not the sign-in page or anything under it, judged on the decoded path

cases.name: characters kept as written
cases.rule: a kept value is returned as written: neither sanitizer re-encodes it

cases.name: encoded double slash
cases.rule: one leading slash: an encoded slash is not a slash, so the value stays a path on this origin

cases.name: trailing space
cases.rule: printable ASCII only: surrounding whitespace is refused, not trimmed

cases.name: delete character
cases.rule: printable ASCII only: DEL is a control character

cases.name: tilde
cases.rule: printable ASCII only: tilde is the last printable character

cases.name: auth page in another case
cases.rule: the sign-in page rule is case-sensitive, as paths are

cases.name: auth page with fragment
cases.rule: not the sign-in page or anything under it, judged on the decoded path
